chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Muhammad ibn Ishaq from 'Ammar al-Nawfali from his father who said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Combing removes the fever (al-waba'), and for Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) there was a comb in the mosque with which he would comb himself whenever he finished from his prayer.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and physical benefit of combing hair according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi links physical grooming to spiritual and physical well-being, with 'al-waba' interpreted by Shia scholars as both epidemic diseases and general fever. It highlights the Prophetic tradition of maintaining cleanliness (taharah) as an act of worship, exemplified by Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) practice of combing his hair in the mosque after prayer, thereby integrating personal hygiene with ritual purity.
